newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold starts higher in nervous European trade.
newsitem.headline: Gold starts higher in nervous European trade.

text.p: Gold and other precious metals opened higher in nervous European trading on Thursday in a technical reaction to recent losses, dealers said.
Gold started at $341.65/$342.15, up from $339.40/$339.90 at the previous close in London, but dealers said the mood was cautious.
"They (metals) are on the way up, although expectations in the market are not very bullish," one trader at a big Swiss bank said.
"There is still talk about range trade, but the range is widening to $338/$343, which expresses the nervousness of the market."
Silver firmed to $4.82/84 from $4.79/$4.81, extending yesterday's gains. Dealers said they expected prices to remain around current levels.
Platinum rose $3.50 to $369.50/$370.50, while palladium advanced $1.75 to $152.50/$153.50.
